problem:
Let $v$ be a non-zero vector from ${R}^{2}$ and let $A$ be the rotation-scaling matrix given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3\sqrt{2} & -3\sqrt{2} \\ 3\sqrt{2} & -3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

The description of $Av$ in terms of geometric transformations in the plane is given below. What are the missing entries?

*To compute the vector $Av$, we rotate $v$ counterclockwise by an angle of $\theta =\text{_____}$ and then scale the result by a factor of $r=\text{_____}.$*
worked_solution:
We can find the scale factor using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{det(A)} \\  & =\sqrt{{(3\sqrt{2})}^{2}+{(3\sqrt{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{18+18} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent $A$ as a product of a rotation and a scaling matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =6[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}r & 0 \\ 0 & r\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain that

$$
{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the missing entries are $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}$ and $r=6.$
